description: Student engineers in third year at Ecole Polytechnique de Thies, in Senegal, our goal is to build a tool so that complex mission data becomes clear, accessible, and useful for everyone. It is all about making an impact : build something useful and worth showing beyond the weekend of the hackathon. Our name are Amadou Sall Ndiaye,Mariama Ndiaye and Papa Mamadou Diop. The latter is in the option IT and telecommunications and the two first in the option aerospace.
summary: TerangaLunar is an interactive mission-planning platform that helps engineers and students select safe landing sites and dates at the lunar South Pole. Near the Moon’s South Pole, the Sun skims the horizon at near-zero angles, meaning even small ridges or crater rims can cast multi-day shadows that drain lander batteries and cut off direct communications with Earth. To solve this critical challenge, TerangaLunar combines real astronomical trajectories from the NASA JPL NAIF & SPICE with high-resolution lunar elevation maps (LOLA) to compute 360° terrain obstruction masks and two-year Sun and Earth visibility forecasts. Delivered through a fast, serverless, bilingual (English/French) web dashboard, it transforms complex orbital physics into intuitive circular horizon radar views, zoomable visibility timelines, and side-by-side site comparisons. Teams can instantly simulate how a launch delay impacts mission survival, check custom power and communication thresholds, find optimal landing windows on a heat-map calendar, and share configurations via direct links. Complete with an educational "Discover" mode featuring guided scenarios, TerangaLunar reduces operational risk and makes lunar exploration planning accessible, reliable, and sustainable.
details:
INTRODUCTION: WHY TerangaLunar?​

Planning a mission to the lunar South Pole comes down to two survival questions: where and when will there be enough sunlight to power the lander, and when can it communicate directly with Earth? Near the Moon’s South Pole, the Sun skims the horizon at near-zero angles, meaning even small crater rims or ridges can cast multi-day shadows that completely change mission feasibility. While astronomical tools already exist, their interfaces are complex and comparing multiple landing sites or launch dates is slow. TerangaLunar bridges the gap between science and engineering by turning complex orbital mechanics and lunar topography into a fast, intuitive, and shareable decision-making platform.

HOW DOES IT WORK

TerangaLunar is an interactive, serverless mission planning platform built for the lunar South Pole. To begin, the user selects a Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) mission, a landing site, an arrival date, and a stay duration. The tool immediately displays where the Sun and Earth appear in the local lunar sky while accounting for the surrounding topography. From this geometry, it extracts clear, vital survival indicators: the percentage of time the site receives sunlight, the longest continuous lunar night the lander must endure, and the exact windows during which direct line of sight communication with Earth is possible.

​Beyond visualization, TerangaLunar actively supports mission decision making. It allows teams to shift the landing date in a single click to simulate schedule delays, identify optimal landing dates on a visual calendar, compare a baseline mission plan side by side against an alternative site, and verify whether a site meets strict operational thresholds such as surviving a continuous lunar night shorter than three days. Every view can be shared via a direct URL link, ensuring scientists and engineers look at the exact same scenario. Finally, an interactive "Discover" mode explains in plain, accessible language why the lunar South Pole is both scientifically exciting and operationally challenging, featuring guided scenarios tailored for students and the general public.

​Under the Hood How Our Algorithm Works:

To deliver instant results in the browser without requiring a heavy backend server, Teranga Lunar prepares the data in three simple steps:

  • ​ mapping the surrounding mountains (360° Horizon Mask): Using NASA LOLA lunar elevation maps (LDEM_80S), our Python script scans 360° around each landing site up to 30 km away while accounting for the Moon’s curvature to measure the exact height of the surrounding hills and crater rims in every direction.
  • ​ tracking the Sun and Earth: We collect precise hourly positions (direction and height in the sky) for both the Sun and Earth over a two year period using the NASA JPL Horizons System.
  • ​ instant visibility check in the browser: For every hour of a selected mission, the web app simply checks whether the Sun or Earth is higher in the sky than the surrounding terrain in that specific direction. If it is higher, the site has sunlight or Earth contact; if it is lower, the terrain blocks it. By adding up these hourly checks over the chosen stay duration, Teranga Lunar instantly calculates total sunlight percentage, the longest continuous shadow period, and whether the site passes the team's safety thresholds.

KEY BENEFITS

  • Instant Mission Clarity in Under Two Seconds: By precomputing two years of NASA JPL NAIF trajectories and 360° lunar terrain masks into ultra lightweight JSON datasets, TerangaLunar eliminates heavy server lag delivering real time, 1 hour resolution solar and Earth visibility intelligence right in the browser, even on mobile devices.
  • Turn Launch Delays into Immediate Action Plans: In spaceflight, schedules slip. Instead of spending hours recalculating orbital mechanics, mission teams can click once to shift a landing date (-7, -1, +1, +7 days), immediately expose multi-day shadow traps, and pivot to safer landing windows on an interactive heat-map calendar.
  • Zero Friction Collaboration Across Teams: With stateless URL encoding, every mission parameter landing site, stay duration, survival thresholds, and language is captured in a single shareable link. Engineers, scientists, and students can open the exact same live scenario on any device with zero login, zero database, and zero privacy footprint.
  • From Raw Astrophysics to Human Intuition: TerangaLunar bridges the gap between expert engineering and public outreach combining strict survival metrics (battery critical lunar nights and communication blackouts) with an interactive, bilingual "Discover" mode that makes South Pole exploration immediately understandable to anyone.

KEY VALUE PROPOSITIONS: WHAT SETS TERANGALUNAR APART

​To stand out from standard astronomical viewers and deliver real world engineering and educational utility, Teranga Lunar brings five high impact value additions:

​1. Rapid Contingency & Crisis Decision Support: Mission planners rarely face ideal conditions; they need to react fast when launch schedules slip. Our side by side "Plan A vs. Plan B" comparator and Mission Feasibility Score (Green/Amber/Red survival indicator based on lander battery and communication profiles) let teams instantly see how a 48 hour delay shifts optimal site selection.

​2. Hardware Aware Mast & Sensor Height Adjustment: Near the lunar South Pole, raising a solar panel or communication antenna by just 2 to 3 meters can clear a distant crater rim. Adding a "Sensor / Mast Height" slider (0 m to 5 m) dynamically adjusts the local horizon obstruction line, reflecting realistic Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) lander constraints.

​3. One-Click "Mission Briefing" & Calendar Exports: Engineering tools create maximum value when they generate actionable deliverables. Userscan export a clean, printable Mission Briefing Report (PDF) containing horizon radar charts, survival metrics, and shareable URLs, as well as downloadable .ics communication schedules for Earth contact windows.

​4. White-Box" Scientific Transparency: Rather than acting as a black box, every dashboard view includes a clear Assumptions & Sources panel documenting exact NASA LOLA terrain resolutions (LDEM_80S), the 30 km lunar curvature ray casting radius, hourly time steps, and model limitations (such as sub pixel micro boulders).

INTENDED IMPACT

​Teranga Lunar serves three complementary audiences:

  1. Mission Planners & Engineers: Accelerating trade-off studies between power generation, thermal survival, and direct-to-Earth communication.
  2. Science & Operations Teams: Coordinating surface operations by tracking low-angle solar illumination (< 5°) and shadow directions.
  3. Students, Educators & the General Public: Demystifying lunar exploration through an interactive "Discover" mode, guided scenarios, and plain-language explanations that show why landing at the lunar South Pole is uniquely challenging.

HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE

  1. Dual Engineering & Science Modes: A single toggle switches the dashboard from engineering survival metrics (power/communications) to scientific surface indicators (shadow azimuths and low-elevation sunlight duration).
  2. ​Pedagogical Storytelling: Instead of presenting raw astronomical tables, we built a bilingual (English/French) "Discover" mode with interactive scenarios (such as simulating a 10-day launch delay or comparing the South Pole to the lunar equator) and inline vocabulary tooltips.
  3. ​Zero-Database Architecture: Encoding full mission states directly into URL hashes provides instant collaboration and printable PDF mission summaries with zero privacy footprint.

BUSINESS MODEL & MONETIZATION STRATEGY

​I. Free Tier (Education, General Public & Open Science)

  • ​Target Audience: Students, educators, independent researchers, and space enthusiasts.
  • Key Features: Open access to predefined landing sites (CLPS missions), the interactive "Discover" educational mode, and standard 2-year visibility forecasts.
  • Strategic Value: Democratizes access to lunar spatial data, fosters an active user community, and drives high visibility among space agencies and academic institutions.

​II. Pro SaaS Subscription (NewSpace Companies & CLPS Operators)

  1. ​Target Audience: Private aerospace companies such as Intuitive Machines, Astrobotic, Firefly Aerospace, designing lunar landers, rovers, or payloads (CLPS commercial partners, space startups).
  2. Premium Features:
  • ​High-Resolution Custom Coordinate Calculations: On-demand generation of ultra-fine horizon masks (meter-scale resolution via LRO NAC data) for any location on the Moon, extending beyond precomputed sites.
  • Advanced Hardware Constraint Modeling: Simulation of exact rover mast heights for solar arrays or antennas (e.g., 2 meters above the lunar surface) paired with precise thermal and power modeling (battery charging curves).
  • API Access & Private Workspaces: Seamless integration of visibility data into internal engineering software suites, featuring role-based access control and strict data confidentiality (eliminating public URL sharing).

​3. Institutional Contracts & Educational Licenses (B2G / B2E)

  • ​Target Audience: Space agencies (NASA, ESA, and emerging agencies such as ASAL or Senegal's upcoming ASES), universities, and planetariums.
  • Offering: White-label software licenses and tailored educational modules featuring mission-training scenarios for future aerospace engineers and science outreach centers.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & DATA USED

To combine scientific rigor with instantaneous web performance, TerangaLunar relies on a streamlined stack of open NASA datasets, scientific Python libraries, and modern serverless web technologies:

  • ​Scientific Data: Official topocentric Sun and Earth ephemerides from the NASA JPL Horizons System and high-resolution Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA LDEM_80S) digital elevation models from NASA’s PDS Geosciences Node.
  • ​Backend Computation: Python 3 with scientific libraries including NumPy, Rasterio (GDAL), and PyProj for coordinate transformations and 360° topographic ray-casting into lightweight JSON datasets.
  • ​Frontend & Visualization: Serverless static web architecture built with HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+), utilizing SVG and HTML5 Canvas for interactive horizon radars, timelines, and instant CSV/image exports.
  • ​Development, Hosting & AI Tools: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) as our primary IDE, GitHub for version control and team collaboration, Firebase for fast serverless web hosting, Freebuff, Claude and DeepSeek to assist with code, debugging, documentation structuring, and bilingual content refinement.

FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED

When designing TerangaLunar, our team carefully balanced scientific accuracy, real-time web performance, and universal usability. Because the Sun skims the horizon at near-zero angles near the lunar South Pole, even a 2° ridge 30 km away can plunge a lander into multi day darkness; therefore, we incorporated lunar curvature into our 30 km topographic ray casting model while optimizing the output into compact JSON datasets so that complex two year profiles load in under two seconds on standard laptops and mobile devices. We also prioritized scientific transparency by embedding an Assumptions & Sources panel directly in every view, clearly documenting data versions, terrain resolution, hourly time steps, and model limitations. Finally, we designed the interface with strict accessibility and inclusion in mind supporting full bilingual switching (English/French), keyboard navigation, high contrast color schemes, and redundant visual patterns so that critical shadow and communication alerts never rely on color alone.
